title: [Audit] 👤 Actor 360
description: One identity’s complete footprint — pick a person in the control bar and every panel becomes their story.

config.content: 👤 **Pick a person in the control bar** and every panel becomes their story; with nobody selected it is the whole estate. **① Is this normal?** is a fixed 7 days in UTC · **② What they did** follows the time picker · **③ Evidence** ends in the raw records. Table times and the session timeline are in your time zone.

config.title: Who this is — events with an email
config.description: Counts only events that carry a user email, so with nobody selected these rows add up to far less than the Events tile: API-key and service traffic with no email behind it has nothing to group on here, and is counted in the tile. The people in range, busiest first — click an email to pin that identity across the suite. `API keys` counts the API keys acting under that email: Elasticsearch stamps a key's CREATOR on every event the key emits, so a person with keys may be carrying a machine's traffic.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.user.email IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*), keys = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.api_key.name, 100) BY attributes.user.email | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 5

config.description: Every audited event for the selection, how many different things that was, and how recently they were last seen. Unfiltered by the noise gate, so it includes connection housekeeping.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | STATS Events = COUNT(*), actions = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.event.action, 100), last_ts = MAX(@timestamp) | EVAL mins = DATE_DIFF("minutes", last_ts, NOW()) | EVAL detail = CASE(Events == 0, "no activity", CONCAT(TO_STRING(actions), CASE(actions == 1, " action", " actions"), " · ", CASE(mins < 1, "just now", mins < 60, CONCAT(TO_STRING(mins), "m ago"), CONCAT(TO_STRING(mins / 60), "h ago")))) | KEEP Events, detail

config.description: Summed severity (weight × events) of everything that scored, how many scoring actions that was, and the highest weight among them (50 is a security config change; the table below names every weight in words). Routine activity scores zero, so this is not an event count in disguise. The receipts are in "Top scoring actions" below: its Risk column adds up to this tile when every scoring action fits the panel, and the count here says how many there are. An action that scored at two weights (a create that succeeded, and one that failed) counts twice, as it is two rows there.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL OR attributes.event.outcome == "failure" OR attributes.event.action IN ("invalidate_apikeys","anonymous_access_denied") OR (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) | STATS n = COUNT(*) BY attributes.event.action, scc = attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL, attributes.event.outcome, resource.attributes.service.name, et = MV_CONCAT(attributes.event.type, ",") | EVAL attributes.event.type = SPLIT(et, ","), attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change = CASE(scc, "present") | EVAL risk = CASE(attributes.event.action == "invalidate_apikeys", 45, attributes.event.action == "anonymous_access_denied", 35, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL, 50, attributes.event.outcome == "failure", 40, (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) AND attributes.event.action IN ("workflow_run","workflow_test","workflow_execution_cancel"), 10, (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) AND (attributes.event.type == "deletion" OR attributes.event.action == "rule_disable"), 30, (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))), 25, 0) | WHERE risk > 0 | STATS sev = SUM(risk * n) BY attributes.event.action, risk | STATS Risk = SUM(sev), worst = MAX(risk), kinds = COUNT(*) | EVAL detail = CASE(worst IS NULL, "nothing scored", CONCAT(TO_STRING(kinds), CASE(kinds == 1, " action · worst ", " actions · worst "), TO_STRING(worst))), Risk = COALESCE(Risk, 0) | KEEP Risk, detail

config.description: The width of their reach in Elasticsearch: index families named in their requests, and how many distinct indices those families hold. A family folds dated daily indices and data-stream backing indices together, as "What they read, by index family" does, so one dashboard reading thirty days of a daily index is one family. Request patterns such as * and date-math names are not counted.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | STATS idx = VALUES(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices) | MV_EXPAND idx | EVAL name = CASE(LOCATE(idx, "*") > 0 OR STARTS_WITH(idx, "<"), null, idx) | EVAL family = REPLACE(REPLACE(name, """^\.ds-""", ""), """[-.]?\d{4}[.-]\d{2}[.-]\d{2}(-\d+)?$""", "") | STATS `Index families` = COUNT_DISTINCT(family), names = COUNT_DISTINCT(name) | EVAL detail = CASE(names == 0, "no index named", CONCAT("from ", TO_STRING(names), CASE(names == 1, " index", " indices"))) | KEEP `Index families`, detail

config.description: Distinct real client addresses — the rows of "Busiest addresses they used" below — how many countries they resolve to, and how many cannot be placed at all, which is always the case for a private or CGNAT address. Many addresses for one named person is the shared-credential signal.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE client.ip IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*), country = MAX(client.geo.country_name), city = MAX(client.geo.city_name), placed = COUNT(client.geo.country_iso_code) BY client.ip | STATS `Client IPs` = COUNT(*), countries = COUNT_DISTINCT(country), unplaced = SUM(CASE(placed == 0, 1, 0)) | EVAL detail = CASE(`Client IPs` == 0, "no client address", CONCAT(TO_STRING(countries), CASE(countries == 1, " country · ", " countries · "), TO_STRING(unplaced), " unplaced")) | KEEP `Client IPs`, detail

config.content: #### ① Is this normal? · _fixed 7-day window in UTC — ignores the time picker_

config.title: Is this normal for them? — hourly, last 7 days (UTC)
config.description: Hourly activity for the current selection against its OWN pattern for that hour of day. The shaded band is their typical range for the hour — the middle half of the seven observations in the window — and a point marks an hour beyond 1.5× that range, which is unusual for them. Seven observations per hour slot is thin, so read it as a sanity check rather than a detector: an identity with a steady background process plus human bursts will sit outside often, and correctly. The headline reads the last complete hour; the current partial hour is left off so it cannot read as a drop. Hours are UTC. Fixed 7-day window: does not follow the time picker. No noise gate, so it will not reconcile with Signal events.

config.title: Where they rank — last 7 days
config.description: The 40 busiest identities by user email over the last 7 days, placed by percentile rank on three measures: how much they did, how many different things they did, and how many kinds of Kibana object they touched. The cohort follows the Project control and nothing else: the people it ranks against are everyone active in the projects in scope, so a Person or Client IP selection highlights that identity (an orange diamond, drawn only when exactly one identity is in scope) instead of shrinking the cohort to one. The projects in scope are the projects the current selection is active in. When that is every project the ranks are exact; when it is one project they are exact for that project; when it is several, events are summed across them and the two distinct counts take the largest per-project value, which can undercount, so the title says approximate. Rank rather than raw value so all three measures share one honest axis: a person can be busier than 90% of the cohort while touching fewer kinds of object than most. Hover any point for its raw numbers. With fewer than two identities there is no rank to draw, and the panel says so instead of plotting one. Fixed 7-day window: does not follow the time picker.

config.title: Working rhythm — last 7 days (UTC)
config.description: Every audited event for the current selection by hour of day and day of week, over the last 7 days in UTC — one cell is one specific hour, not an average, because a seven-day window holds each hour of the week exactly once. Strength is volume on a log scale, so a quiet hour stays visible beside a busy one; a bare grey slot is an hour with no events at all. Fixed window: this panel does not follow the time picker. No noise gate: it measures presence, so it will not reconcile with Signal events. UTC is stated rather than localised so the chart reads the same for every viewer, whatever their timezone — read the rhythm, not the clock.

config.content: #### ② What they did · _follows the time picker · times in your time zone_

config.title: How they reached what they touched in Kibana — credential → space → object → operation
config.description: How the current selection's Kibana activity flows: which credential it arrived with, which space it happened in, what kind of object it touched and what it did to it. Ribbon width is event count in the time picker's range. Kibana audit only, and only events that touched an object — requests, logins and point-in-time internals are left out. Elasticsearch events carry no space and no saved object, so including them would put most of the ink in a branch that says nothing. Credential is authentication type where Elasticsearch records one and the user's realm otherwise, which is what separates a person in a browser (SAML SSO, the cloud-saml-kibana realm) from a script calling Kibana with a key (Elasticsearch or Cloud API key); hover a credential for its raw name. Object types come from the shared OBJ_TYPE fragment, which recovers a type from the event for workflows, ML jobs, agent-builder tools and secrets that carry no saved-object fields. Top 40 flows: a missing ribbon means the flow is outside the top 40, not that it never happened. Each column names its biggest values and folds the rest into "other (N)", drawn last, so a small value is counted there rather than drawn as an unlabelled sliver. Click a named credential or space to pin it across the suite — object type and operation are derived, so a pill on them would match nothing. Double-click anywhere in the panel to clear every pill on the page.

config.title: ⚠️ What they changed
config.description: Everything they changed, ran or deleted in Kibana — newest first. `type` and `name` are the real saved-object fields where Kibana records them, and are otherwise recovered from the event message: workflows, agent-builder agents and tools, ML jobs and secrets carry no saved_object fields at all. A workflow run, test or cancel carries its run on the name ("· run" and the first 8 characters of the run id) — a cancel and the run it cancelled share that id; the full id is in the session records at the bottom of the page. `result` reads "attempted" where Kibana logged the attempt rather than the outcome; "failure" is a change that was denied.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) | GROK body.text """\[(?:id|workflowId)=%{DATA:g_id}(?:,|\])""" | GROK body.text """\[name=%{GREEDYDATA:g_name}\]""" | GROK body.text """\[executionId=%{DATA:g_exec}\]""" | GROK body.text """case id: %{NOTSPACE:g_case}""" | GROK body.text """(?:job|datafeed) %{NOTSPACE:g_ml}""" | EVAL obj_name = COALESCE(attributes.kibana.saved_object.name, g_name, g_id, attributes.kibana.saved_object.id, g_case, g_ml, g_exec, body.text) | EVAL result = CASE(attributes.event.outcome == "unknown", "attempted", attributes.event.outcome) | EVAL execution = COALESCE(LEFT(g_exec, 8), "—") | STATS n = COUNT(*), last_ts = MAX(@timestamp) BY attributes.event.action, attributes.kibana.saved_object.type, obj_name, execution, space = attributes.kibana.space.id, result | EVAL verb = CASE(attributes.event.action LIKE "*_execution_cancel", "cancel", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_run_soon", "run", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_run", "run", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_test", "test", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_enable", "enable", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_disable", "disable", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_put_*", "create", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_open_*", "open", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_start_*", "start", attributes.event.action LIKE "*point_in_time", "pit", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_create*", "create", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_update*", "update", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_delete", "delete", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_find", "find", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_get", "get", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_resolve", "resolve", "other") | EVAL obj_type = CASE(attributes.kibana.saved_object.type IS NOT NULL, attributes.kibana.saved_object.type, attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_*ad_job", "ml-job", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_*ad_datafeed", "ml-datafeed", attributes.event.action LIKE "workflow_execution_*", "workflow-execution", attributes.event.action LIKE "workflow_*", "workflow", attributes.event.action LIKE "agent_builder_agent_*", "agent-builder-agent", attributes.event.action LIKE "agent_builder_tool_*", "agent-builder-tool", attributes.event.action LIKE "product_documentation_*", "product-documentation", attributes.event.action == "secret_create", "secret", attributes.event.action IS NULL, "unclassified", REPLACE(attributes.event.action, "_(create|update|delete|enable|disable|run|run_soon|test|cancel)$", "")) | STATS events = SUM(n), last_seen = MAX(last_ts) BY verb, type = obj_type, name = obj_name, execution, space, result | EVAL name = CASE(execution == "—", name, CONCAT(name, " · run ", execution)), type = REPLACE(type, "-", " ") | DROP execution | SORT last_seen DESC | LIMIT 10

config.title: What they read, by index family
config.description: Where their reads concentrate, busiest first. Dated daily indices and data-stream backing indices are folded into the family they belong to, so a date-suffixed series is one row and `Indices` says how many of its members were read. A request naming several indices counts once per index; request patterns such as * and date-math names are left out. The audit stream itself usually tops the list, because every dashboard on this page reads it.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices IS NOT NULL | MV_EXPAND attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices | STATS n = COUNT(*) BY attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices | WHERE NOT (LOCATE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, "*") > 0 OR STARTS_WITH(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, "<")) | EVAL family = REPLACE(REPLACE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, """^\.ds-""", ""), """[-.]?\d{4}[.-]\d{2}[.-]\d{2}(-\d+)?$""", "") | STATS events = SUM(n), indices = COUNT(*) BY family | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 9

config.title: ⚠️ System and hidden index reads · none is good
config.description: Dot-prefixed indices — system and hidden — that their requests named, one row per index family: daily indices of the same stream are folded together and `Indices` says how many were touched. The index shown is one real member of the family — the row counts the whole family — and it is what a click pins; then "Open in Elasticsearch Data Access" to see who else reads it. Data-stream backing indices (.ds-*) are left out; they are ordinary data. An empty panel means nothing matched in the time range, which is the healthy state.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices IS NOT NULL | MV_EXPAND attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".*" AND NOT attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".ds-*" | STATS n = COUNT(*), seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, action = attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action | EVAL family = REPLACE(REPLACE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, """^\.ds-""", ""), """[-.]?\d{4}[.-]\d{2}[.-]\d{2}(-\d+)?$""", "") | STATS events = SUM(n), indices = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices), actions = COUNT_DISTINCT(action), last_seen = MAX(seen), `attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices` = MIN(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices) BY family | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 9

config.title: Where they connected from
config.description: Where the current selection connected from, in the time picker's range. Points are resolved client locations sized by event volume; a line joins one location to the next the same identity appeared from, colored by the speed that move implies between last seen there and first seen here. Places are aggregated per city, so an identity active in two cities at overlapping times is marked as such rather than given an impossible speed. Read the title line first: many events cannot be placed at all — an address geoip never placed (always the case for CGNAT and private addresses), an event with no client IP, or an event from a placeable address that predates geo enrichment — so the absence of a line is not evidence of absence. An address counts as unplaceable only when none of its events were placed, as in "Busiest addresses they used". The line legend appears only when there is a line to read. This is a movement record, not an impossible-travel detector.

config.title: Busiest addresses they used
config.description: Their real client addresses, busiest first, one row per address — the same addresses the Client IPs tile counts — including the ones the map cannot show. "unplaced" means geoip placed none of that address's events, which is always the case for a private or CGNAT address; "—" is a country with no city. An address keeps its place even when some of its events predate geo enrichment. Click an address to pin it, then "Open in Geo & Network".

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE client.ip IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp), country = MAX(client.geo.country_name), city = MAX(client.geo.city_name), placed = COUNT(client.geo.country_iso_code) BY client.ip | EVAL city = CASE(placed == 0, "unplaced", COALESCE(city, "—")), country = CASE(placed == 0, "unplaced", country) | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 10

config.title: Top scoring actions, with their weight
config.description: The biggest contributors to the Risk tile, largest first: Risk here is weight × events, and every scoring action together adds up to the tile. The tile's subtitle says how many scoring actions there are; any beyond the last row here are the smallest. Click an action to pin it, then "Open in Security & Anomalies" to see who else does it — the pinned person and action combine, so clear the person pill first to compare.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL OR attributes.event.outcome == "failure" OR attributes.event.action IN ("invalidate_apikeys","anonymous_access_denied") OR (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) | STATS n = COUNT(*), last_ts = MAX(@timestamp) BY attributes.event.action, scc = attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL, attributes.event.outcome, resource.attributes.service.name, et = MV_CONCAT(attributes.event.type, ",") | EVAL attributes.event.type = SPLIT(et, ","), attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change = CASE(scc, "present") | EVAL risk = CASE(attributes.event.action == "invalidate_apikeys", 45, attributes.event.action == "anonymous_access_denied", 35, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL, 50, attributes.event.outcome == "failure", 40, (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) AND attributes.event.action IN ("workflow_run","workflow_test","workflow_execution_cancel"), 10, (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) AND (attributes.event.type == "deletion" OR attributes.event.action == "rule_disable"), 30, (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))), 25, 0) | WHERE risk > 0 | STATS events = SUM(n), severity = SUM(risk * n), last_seen = MAX(last_ts) BY attributes.event.action, weight = risk | EVAL why = CASE(weight == 50, "security config change", weight == 45, "API keys invalidated", weight == 40, "failed or denied", weight == 35, "anonymous request denied", weight == 30, "destructive Kibana change", weight == 25, "Kibana change", weight == 10, "workflow execution", "scored") | SORT severity DESC | LIMIT 8

config.content: #### ③ Evidence · _session timeline is fixed at 24 hours · the records follow the time picker · your time zone_

config.title: Kibana sessions — last 24 hours, your time zone
config.description: One bar per Kibana browser session in the last 24 hours, newest first — its length runs from the first to the last thing they did in it and its strength is how much it did, which are independent: a short session can carry far more activity than a long one left open and idle. Click a bar to set the dashboard's time range to that session (plus a minute either side); use the time picker's back arrow to return. Shift-click pins that identity across the suite. What an open browser tab does on its own — internal page requests, usage counters, point-in-time paging — is left out, exactly as in the Session records below, so a tab left open does not stretch a bar past the person's last action and every bar has records under it. Only Kibana audit carries a session id, so an identity that works through the Elasticsearch API has no sessions, and an empty panel for it is the correct answer. Twelve most recent sessions, each labelled with who and when it started. Times are in your browser's timezone, like the rest of Kibana. Fixed 24-hour window: does not follow the time picker.

config.title: Session records · often empty at 1h
config.description: The raw Kibana events behind the session timeline above, newest first, with full session and object ids and the message Kibana wrote. Like the timeline, it leaves out what an open browser tab does on its own — internal page requests, usage counters, point-in-time paging — so a session in the timeline always has records here, and an hour in which they only had Kibana open is empty. An Identity that reads as an opaque id is a principal whose events carry no email and no key name — usually an organisation-level Elastic Cloud API key, which the audit stream records only by its id. Often empty over the default hour on a healthy project; widen the time range to see older rows.
